title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and its neighbours). A set E carries a 'disposition': a symmetric relation x|o|y, read as 'x and y are disjoint', or orthogonal. For subsets, A|o|B means a|o|b for all a in A and b in B.

There are two polar operators:
- cosupp°_E(A) = {x | x|o|A}, the orthogonal of A;
- supp°_E(A) = cosupp°(cosupp°(A)), the double orthogonal, a closure operator.

Σ_E is the set of closed subsets. With C·B := cosupp°(B), it is the complete ortholattice of a polarity. In modern terms this is an orthogonality space (orthoset) and its lattice of biorthogonally closed sets.

Given a map α: E→E' that is 'compatible with dispositions', define:
- ᾱ = direct image on subsets;
- α_*: Σ_E→Σ_E', with α_*(B) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(B)).

The previous page reduces the statement 'α_* commutes with orthocomplement C' to a key formula (**). For B in Σ_E and C = cosupp°_E(B), (**) reads supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(C)) = cosupp°_{E'}(ᾱ(B)).

One inclusion is already done. It amounts to ᾱ(C)|o|ᾱ(B), which follows from B|o|_E C and the compatibility of α (orthogonality is preserved).

On this page Grothendieck isolates the remaining inclusion, cosupp°_{E'}(ᾱ(B)) ⊂ supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(C)). Unwound, it says: for x', y' in E', if x'|o|ᾱ(B) and y'|o|ᾱ(C), then x'|o|y'.

He observes that preservation of orthogonality cannot give this. That hypothesis only controls the disposition of points of E' that lie in the image of E, whereas x' and y' are arbitrary. He gives an immediate counterexample with the 'tautological disposition' x|o|y ⇔ x≠y:
- here Σ_E = P(E) and Σ_E' = P(E');
- compatibility of α means α is injective;
- α_*(A) = α(A);
- α_* commutes with complement only if α is also surjective, i.e. bijective (completed on the next page).

The next page then adds a backward correspondence β: E'→P(E), with the condition ᾱ(β(x')) ⊂ supp°({x'}) plus a fidelity condition on ᾱ for |o|. This is a kind of adjoint making α_* an ortholattice morphism.

Problem served: building a category of 'dispositions' whose morphisms induce orthocomplement-preserving maps of the associated closed-set lattices. This is a functoriality question for polarities and ortholattices.
errors: No mathematical error. The counterexample is correct: in the Boolean case, α(E∖A) = E'∖α(A) for all A forces α(E) = E' (take A = ∅), and injectivity then gives bijectivity.
Minor point: the conclusion 'n'est compatible à C que si α surjective' is stated without proof, but it is immediate as above.

ideas.what: Set with a symmetric 'disjointness' relation (disposition), polar operators cosupp°/supp°, lattice Σ_E of biorthogonally closed sets with orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space / orthoset; polarity (Birkhoff) and its complete ortholattice of closed sets

ideas.what: Reduction of 'α_* commutes with orthocomplement' to a pointwise condition on E', and recognition that mere preservation of orthogonality is insufficient
ideas.modern_name: morphisms of orthosets / ortholattice homomorphisms induced by maps

ideas.what: Counterexample via the tautological disposition x⊥y ⇔ x≠y, giving Σ = power set; compatible maps are the injections, and complement-preservation forces bijectivity

missed.claim: Grothendieck's search for a backward correspondence β: E'→P(E) to make α_* orthocomplement-preserving (next page) parallels the much later notion of adjointable maps between orthosets. These are maps f, g with f(x)⊥y ⇔ x⊥g(y), studied in recent quantum-logic work on categories of orthogonality spaces. The 1986 notes appear to anticipate the same functoriality problem independently.
missed.quote: Il ne semble pas que ceci puisse se déduire de la seule compatibilité de α aux dispositions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working on orthogonality-space functoriality. The mathematics itself is elementary and has been developed since.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary lemma-and-counterexample about polarities and orthocomplements. Interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's 1986 'dispositions' formalism, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The displayed question should read cosupp°_{E'}(ᾱ(B)) ⊂ supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(C)), not 'conv°'/'inv°'. This matches the notation of the previous page and of the derivation itself.
The first line likely continues the previous page's 'et résulte de B|o|_E C, compte tenu de la compatibilité de α aux dispositions' rather than 'connote donc de la'. The opening word is uncertain.
The marginal note reads approximately 'Mais, en effet, voir plus bas'.
